subject: Clarify DPA: incident notification windows, scope and subprocessor obligations
messages:
From: Claire Huang <security@brightbank.com>

Cc: Marco Rossi <procurement@brightbank.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification needed on DPA incident notification clauses

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. As we prepare to finalize the DPA we noticed some ambiguity around the incident notification section and subprocessors that we need clarified before Legal signs off. High-level asks:

- Notification timing: our security team prefers a 24-hour substantive notification for incidents affecting customer data. Your DPA currently references "prompt" and a separate 72-hour obligation for evidence handover in an SOW. Can you confirm what Redwood will commit to as a binding contractual timeline (acknowledgement vs substantive details vs evidence handoff)?

- Scope of notice: we need to know whether notifications will include affected tenant identifiers, sample logs, and initial root-cause indicators. If Redwood redacts samples due to multi-tenant considerations, we need a defined redaction policy.

- Subprocessor coordination: can you confirm Redwood's expectations for subprocessors when an incident affects a subprocessor? Will Redwood require subprocessors to meet the same notification windows or will Redwood act as the single notifier?

- International transfers & regulators: some of our customers are in EMEA and APAC; regulators may require immediate filing with local authorities. We need a clause that allows BrightBank to comply with regulatory obligations while preserving Redwood's limited forensic access cadence.

I've attached a redline of the DPA with comments (BrightBank_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Please coordinate with Legal and Security and come back with proposed contract language and an operational timeline we can sign up to.

Appreciate the help — Claire

--

Irene / Kim,

Draft proposal below — goal is to be commercially reasonable for BrightBank while protecting multi-tenant ops and not promising instant forensic exports we can't guarantee. I've also attached a simple CSV timeline (proposed-notify-timeline.csv) for the SOW.

Operational/staged notification (proposed):
1) Acknowledgement (T0 + 6 hours): Redwood will send an acknowledgement that we have detected/received an incident report and confirm whether the incident is under investigation. This acknowledgement will not contain PII or tenant-specific forensic evidence.
2) Initial notification (T0 + 24 hours): Redwood will provide a summary of scope (affected product modules and, where available, tenant identifiers impacted). If tenant identifiers are unavailable due to ongoing triage, Redwood will state that scope assessment is in progress and provide estimated time to scope.
3) Scoped technical update (T0 + 48–72 hours): Provide technical indicators (logs, redacted samples, root-cause hypothesis) as available. Where multi-tenant data requires redaction, Redwood will include a redaction rationale and a redaction policy pointer.
4) Evidence handover & forensic access (T0 + up to 7 days): Forensic artifacts and exports (snapshots, queryable logs where permitted) will be handed over on request within seven calendar days, subject to customer access controls and export approvals.

Contract language suggestions (short snippets we can propose in DPA):
- "Acknowledgement: Redwood will acknowledge receipt of an incident report within six hours of detection or notification and will indicate whether an investigation is underway."
- "Initial Notification: Subject to investigator safety and legal restrictions, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide an initial notification describing the nature of the incident and, where known, the impacted customer tenant identifiers within 24 hours of confirmation of an incident affecting customer data."
- "Forensic Handover: Redwood will provide forensic artifacts or exports upon customer request within seven calendar days of an incident confirmation, unless restricted by applicable law or required regulatory filings. Redwood will make reasonable efforts to coordinate subprocessors to facilitate evidence access; where subprocessors retain exclusive custody of evidence, Redwood will act as the primary liaison and will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain evidence from the subprocessor."

Subprocessor commitments:
- We should offer to require subprocessors to adopt the same acknowledgement and initial-notify timelines (6/24) in our subproc agreements for BrightBank-covered customers. For third-party infra providers where we cannot impose terms, we commit to act as primary notifier and to escalate to the customer if subproc timelines cause delay.

Compliance/regulatory carveouts:
- Add explicit clause: "Notwithstanding the foregoing timelines, Redwood will comply with applicable laws and regulatory obligations which may require longer or shorter notice periods; in such cases Redwood will provide the customer and regulators the notices required by law and will notify the customer if regulatory obligations impact forensic handover timing."

If this looks good I can send to Claire and propose the staged approach + clause snippets.

Ben
Senior Manager, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Irene / Ben / Kim —

Thanks for the thoughtful proposal, Ben. BrightBank security can accept the proposed staged-notify cadence (6h ack, 24h initial notification, 48–72h scoped technical update, forensic handover within 7 days) as long as the following are added to the DPA:

- Regulatory override language that allows immediate filings by BrightBank when required by law (we will notify Redwood prior to filing when practicable).
- Explicit subprocessor obligation: either Redwood must ensure BrightBank-covered workloads carry identical notification SLAs with subprocessors, or Redwood must include a governance clause committing to use all reasonable contractual and operational levers to obtain evidence from subprocessors within the same timeframes and to escalate delays to BrightBank.
- Redaction policy appendix: brief pointer to a redaction appendix that defines what is redacted, why, and how to request full unredacted evidence under a protected-access process.

If Redwood can provide a redlined DPA incorporating the staged language and the three bullets above, Procurement is ready to update the DocuSign envelope and we can route for signature. See the DocuSign link below for the existing envelope.

DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/embeddedSigning?token=EXAMPLE-DS-48291
